arxiv-2010-02293.title: Using Soft Actor-Critic for Low-Level UAV Control
arxiv-2010-02293.creator: Gabriel M. Barros, Esther L. Colombini
arxiv-2010-02293.description: Abstract Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs), or drones, have recently been used in several civil application domains from organ delivery to remote locations to wireless network coverage. These platforms, however, are naturally unstable systems for which many different control approaches have been proposed. Generally based on classic and modern control, these algorithms require knowledge of the robot’s dynamics.

arxiv-2205-13691.title: Suppression of Peierls-like, nesting-based instabilities in solids
arxiv-2205-13691.creator: Nassim Derriche, Ilya Elfimov, George Sawatzky
arxiv-2205-13691.description: Abstract Understanding instabilities is of vast importance in material science. One such example is the Peierls instability of one-dimensional metals with a single band. The question is why H and Li chains behave so differently in spite of their similar electronic structure.

arxiv-2211-13025.title: Continuous Deformations of Algebras of Holomorphic Functions on Subvarieties of a Noncommutative Ball
arxiv-2211-13025.creator: Maria Dmitrieva
arxiv-2211-13025.description: Abstract \vskip-12.0pt We propose a general method for constructing continuous Banach bundles whose fibers are algebras of holomorphic functions on subvarieties of a closed noncommutative ball. These algebras are of the form 𝒜 d / I x \mathcal{A}_{d}/I_{x} , where 𝒜 d \mathcal{A}_{d} is the noncommutative disk algebra introduced by G.

arxiv-2309-15289.title: SEPT: Towards Efficient Scene Representation Learning for Motion Prediction
arxiv-2309-15289.creator: Zhiqian Lan, Yuxuan Jiang, Yao Mu, Chen Chen, Shengbo Eben LiSchool of Vehicle and Mobility, Tsinghua University {lanzq21, jyx21}@mails.tsinghua.edu.cnlishbo@tsinghua.edu.cn
arxiv-2309-15289.description: Abstract Motion prediction is crucial for autonomous vehicles to operate safely in complex traffic environments. Extracting effective spatiotemporal relationships among traffic elements is key to accurate forecasting. Inspired by the successful practice of pretrained large language models, this paper presents SEPT, a modeling framework that leverages self-supervised learning to develop powerful spatiotemporal understanding for complex traffic scenes.

arxiv-2404-05938.title: Neural networks can be FLOP-efficient integrators of 1D oscillatory integrands
arxiv-2404-05938.creator: Anshuman Sinha, Spencer H. Bryngelson shb@gatech.edu
arxiv-2404-05938.description: Abstract We demonstrate that neural networks can be FLOP-efficient integrators of one-dimensional oscillatory integrands. We train a feed-forward neural network to compute integrals of highly oscillatory 1D functions. The training set is a parametric combination of functions with varying characters and oscillatory behavior degrees.

arxiv-2501-12884.title: Learning Graph Node Embeddings by Smooth Pair Sampling
arxiv-2501-12884.creator: Konstantin Kutzkov
arxiv-2501-12884.description: Abstract Random walk-based node embedding algorithms have attracted a lot of attention due to their scalability and ease of implementation. Previous research has focused on different walk strategies, optimization objectives, and embedding learning models. Inspired by observations on real data, we take a different approach and propose a new regularization technique.

arxiv-2504-09759.title: Enhancing Classifier Evaluation: A Fairer Benchmarking Strategy Based on Ability and Robustness
arxiv-2504-09759.creator: Lucas Felipe Ferraro Cardoso, Vitor Cirilo Araujo Santos, José de Sousa Ribeiro Filho, Regiane Silva Kawasaki Francês, Ricardo Bastos Cavalcante Prudêncio, Ronnie Cley de Oliveira Alves
arxiv-2504-09759.description: Abstract Benchmarking is a fundamental practice in machine learning (ML) for comparing the performance of classification algorithms. However, traditional evaluation methods often overlook a critical aspect: the joint consideration of dataset complexity and an algorithm’s ability to generalize. Without this dual perspective, assessments may favor models that perform well on easy instances while failing to capture their true robustness.

arxiv-2509-22876.title: HEART: Emotionally-driven test-time scaling of Language Models
arxiv-2509-22876.creator: Gabriela Pinto, Palash Goyal, Yiwen Song, Souradip Chakraborty, Zifeng Wang, Tomas Pfister, Hamid Palangi
arxiv-2509-22876.description: Abstract Test-time scaling has shown considerable success in improving the performance of language models on complex reasoning tasks without requiring fine-tuning. However, current strategies such as self-reflection primarily focus on logical or structural refinement. They do not leverage the guiding potential of affective feedback.

arxiv-2601-13318.title: Structured eigenbases and pair state transfer on threshold graphs
arxiv-2601-13318.creator: Leonardo de Lima, Renata Del-Vecchio, Hermie Monterde, Heber Teixeira
arxiv-2601-13318.description: Abstract Recently, Macharete, Del-Vecchio, Teixeira and de Lima showed that a star and any threshold graph on the same number of vertices share the same eigenbasis relative to the Laplacian matrix. britannica-1911-marie-louise.title: Marie Louise (1911 Encyclopaedia Britannica article)
britannica-1911-marie-louise.creator: Encyclopaedia Britannica
britannica-1911-marie-louise.description: Article 'Marie Louise' from the 1911 Encyclopædia Britannica (Volume 17), the classic English-language general encyclopedia, now in the public domain. was the daughter of Francis I., emperor of Austria, and of the princess Theresa of Naples, and was born on the 12th of December 1791. Her disposition, fresh and natural but lacking the qualities that make for distinction, gave no promise of eminence until reasons of state brought Napoleon shortly after his divorce of Josephine to sue for her hand (see Napoleon and Josephine).

pmc-10553835.title: Spatial regulation of Drosophila ovarian Follicle Stem Cell division rates and cell cycle transitions
pmc-10553835.creator: David Melamed, Aaron Choi, Amy Reilein, Simon Tavaré, Daniel Kalderon, Ken M. Cadigan, Gregory P. Copenhaver, Ken M. Cadigan, Gregory P. Copenhaver, Ken M. Cadigan, Gregory P. Copenhaver, Ken M. Cadigan, Gregory P. Copenhaver
pmc-10553835.description: Drosophila ovarian Follicle Stem Cells (FSCs) present a favorable paradigm for understanding how stem cell division and differentiation are balanced in communities where those activities are independent. FSCs also allow exploration of how this balance is integrated with spatial stem cell heterogeneity.

pmc-10689460.title: Enhancing robot evolution through Lamarckian principles
pmc-10689460.creator: Jie Luo, Karine Miras, Jakub Tomczak, Agoston E. Eiben
pmc-10689460.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). Evolutionary robot systems offer two principal advantages: an advanced way of developing robots through evolutionary optimization and a special research platform to conduct what-if experiments regarding questions about evolution. Our study sits at the intersection of these.

pmc-11349707.title: Bulimia nervosa and treatment-related disparities: a review
pmc-11349707.creator: Kim Wilson, Robert Kagabo
pmc-11349707.description: IntroductionBulimia nervosa (BN) is a type of eating disorder disease usually manifesting between adolescence and early adulthood with 12 as median age of onset. BN is characterized by individuals’ episodes of excessive eating of food followed by engaging in unusual compensatory behaviors to control weight gain in BN. Approximately 94% of those with BN never seek or delay treatment.

pmc-11357388.title: Advances in Intrathecal Nanoparticle Delivery: Targeting the Blood–Cerebrospinal Fluid Barrier for Enhanced CNS Drug Delivery
pmc-11357388.creator: Ahmad Khalid Madadi, Moon-Jun Sohn
pmc-11357388.description: The blood–cerebrospinal fluid barrier (BCSFB) tightly regulates molecular exchanges between the bloodstream and cerebrospinal fluid (CSF), creating challenges for effective central nervous system (CNS) drug delivery. This review assesses intrathecal (IT) nanoparticle (NP) delivery systems that aim to enhance drug delivery by circumventing the BCSFB, complementing approaches that target the blood–brain barrier (BBB).

pmc-11640336.title: Development of a Simple IFN-γ Release Whole Blood Assay for the Assessment of Leishmania infantum Specific Cellular Immunity in Dogs
pmc-11640336.creator: Anna Sára Molnár, Andrea Murillo-Picco, Clara Jiménez-Fortunato, Laia Solano-Gallego
pmc-11640336.description: Simple SummaryCanine leishmaniosis (CanL) is a zoonotic disease caused by a parasite that can be transmitted by a mosquito-like insect called a sandfly. In dogs, the disease can range from mild to very severe, depending on the state of the dog’s immune system. For this reason, it is important to detect the infection early.

pmc-12592957.title: Timing of Vasopressin Initiation in Patients with Septic Shock: An Updated Systematic Review and Meta-analysis with Trial Sequential Analysis
pmc-12592957.creator: Anirban Bhattacharjee, Priyankar K Datta, Vivek Kumar, Rajathadri H Ravikumar, Prachee Sathe, Riddhi Kundu
pmc-12592957.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Background and aimsWe performed this systematic review and meta-analysis to study the timing of vasopressin initiation and its association with patient-centered outcomes in adult patients with septic shock.Data sources and study selectionWe searched Embase, PubMed, and Web of Science for eligible prospective, retrospective studies, and Randomized controlled trials (RCTs) from January 2013 to December 2024 in adult patients with septic shock that compared an early (<6 hours) vs late strategy (>6 hours) of vasopressin initiation.

pmc-12689817.title: Real-world outcomes of robotic and non-robotic hysterectomy for endometrial cancer: insights from a national cohort
pmc-12689817.creator: Hui-Hsuan Lau, Yu-san Chien, Jiun-Yi Li, Ching-Hu Chung
pmc-12689817.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). To compare perioperative outcomes, postoperative complications, and overall survival among patients with endometrial cancer (EC) undergoing open hysterectomy (OH), laparoscopic hysterectomy (LH), or robot-assisted hysterectomy (RAH) using nationwide real-world data. This was a retrospective, population-based study using 2018–2020 Taiwan Cancer Registry who underwent one of three surgical approaches (open, laparoscopic, or robot-assisted) and outcomes were evaluated using NHIRD with follow-up data available through 2021.

pmc-12729773.title: Integrated Antioxidants, Nanoparticle, and Antifreeze Protein Strategies Synergistically Enhance Cryotop Vitrification Outcomes of Porcine Parthenogenetic Embryos
pmc-12729773.creator: Jesse Oluwaseun Ayantoye, Baigao Yang, Jianhua Dong, Xiaoyi Feng, Muhammad Shahzad, Hubdar Ali Kolachi, Pengcheng Wan, Hongmei Pan, Xueming Zhao, Cinzia Domenicotti
pmc-12729773.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Porcine embryo cryopreservation remains challenging due to high lipid content, oxidative stress, and ice recrystallization that compromise post-thaw survival and developmental competence. We evaluated an integrated vitrification approach combining antioxidants (berberine, melatonin), iron oxide (Fe3O4) nanoparticles, and antifreeze protein I (AFP I) with post-thaw interventions (glutathione and zona pellucida digestion) to synergistically improve cryosurvival and developmental competence of porcine parthenogenetic embryos.

pmc-13558275.title: Efficacy and Safety of a Novel Filtering Function to Reduce Radiation Exposure During Catheter Ablation for Atrial Fibrillation
pmc-13558275.creator: Nobuhiro Suzuki, Hidehiro Iwakawa, Toshiharu Shinohara, Ryosuke Kato, Hiyu Wakabayashi, Ryota Kaimori, Ken Terata, Hiroyuki Watanabe
pmc-13558275.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). BackgroundWe aimed to assess the effectiveness and safety of a new filtering feature (Spot ROITM, Canon Medical Systems, Japan) in reducing radiation exposure during radiofrequency catheter ablation (RFCA) for atrial fibrillation (AF).Methods and ResultsThe study involved 2 steps: (1) an ex vivo experiment to evaluate the radiation reduction of Spot ROITM (SROI); (2) a clinical study with 69 consecutive patients undergoing initial AF-RFCA, divided into conventional collimation (CC) and SROI groups. All procedures used 3-dimensional electroanatomical mapping guidance.

pmc-13668390.title: Dual Use of Electronic and Combustible Cigarettes and Stroke Risk: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis
pmc-13668390.creator: Ah-Ram Sul, Tae-Hyeok Kim, Heejin Kimm, Yu-Jin Paek
pmc-13668390.description: ObjectivesDual use of electronic and combustible cigarettes is increasing, but its association with cardiovascular outcomes, including stroke, remains unclear. This systematic review and meta-analysis evaluated associations of dual use with stroke and other cardiovascular outcomes compared with study-specific reference groups.

pmc-13675099.title: Improving quality of life in cancer patients with an app-based intervention (Mika-App): secondary results from a randomized controlled waitlist-trial in Germany
pmc-13675099.creator: Franziska Springer, Hannah Brock, David Kreilinger, Gandolf Finke, Jan Simon Raue, Anja Mehnert-Theuerkauf
